about.title: Hands-on therapy, not a hand-out sheet
body: Shree Shanmuga Physiotherapy Centre was built around one idea: recovery happens through skilled, hands-on work between therapist and patient, not by handing someone a printed exercise sheet and a follow-up date. Based in Porur, we work with athletes carrying sports injuries, patients recovering from orthopedic surgery, and anyone dealing with joint stiffness or chronic pain that hasn't responded to rest alone.

Every plan starts with a manual assessment of how you actually move, followed by a mix of joint mobilization, soft-tissue work, and progressive loading — reviewed and adjusted session by session rather than locked in on day one.
highlights: Manual therapy and joint mobilization on every visit
Dedicated sports injury and post-surgical recovery tracks
Progress reviewed and adjusted every session, not just monthly

services.name: Sports Injury Rehabilitation
services.tagline: Built around getting back to your sport, not just off the sidelines
services.overview: From ligament sprains to muscle strains and overuse injuries, we combine hands-on manual therapy with progressive strengthening so you return to your sport with confidence, not just clearance.
symptoms: Pain or instability during sport-specific movement
Reduced strength or confidence in the injured area
procedure: Hands-on manual therapy for pain and mobility
benefits: Rehab tailored to your specific sport and position
Hands-on treatment at every visit, not just exercise handouts
Progress tracked against clear strength and mobility benchmarks
services.recovery: Recovery timelines typically run 3–14 weeks depending on injury severity and sport demands.

faqs.question: Can I keep training while I recover?
faqs.answer: In most cases yes — we build modified training into your plan wherever it's safe to keep you moving.

services.name: Post-Surgical Physiotherapy
services.tagline: Structured, phase-based recovery from the day you're cleared for therapy
services.overview: Whether you've had knee, hip, shoulder, or spine surgery, our post-surgical program restores strength and range of motion in structured phases, coordinated with your surgeon's protocol.
symptoms: Stiffness and reduced range of motion after surgery
Difficulty bearing weight or resuming daily activity
benefits: Faster, safer return to daily activity
Reduced risk of stiffness and re-injury
Plan coordinated with your surgeon's recovery protocol
services.recovery: Typical programs run 6–12 weeks depending on the surgery, with progress reviewed every session.

faqs.question: How soon after surgery should I start?
faqs.answer: Most surgeons clear patients for physiotherapy within 1–2 weeks post-surgery — we coordinate with your surgeon's specific protocol before starting.

services.name: Manual Therapy & Joint Mobilization
services.tagline: Hands-on treatment for stiff, painful, or restricted joints
services.overview: Manual therapy is the core of how we treat at Shree Shanmuga Physiotherapy — hands-on joint mobilization and soft-tissue release to restore movement that exercise alone often can't reach.
symptoms: Muscle tightness that doesn't ease with stretching
Restricted range of motion after injury or inactivity
procedure: Manual assessment of joint and soft-tissue restriction
Guided movement to maintain gained range
benefits: Often faster relief than exercise alone for restricted joints
Addresses the specific joint or tissue that's actually restricted
Complements every other program we run
services.recovery: Most patients notice improved range of motion within 2–4 sessions.

services.name: Chronic Back & Neck Pain Treatment
services.tagline: Relief that addresses the cause, not just the symptom
services.overview: Long-standing back and neck pain is often driven by posture, muscle imbalance, or an old injury pattern. We assess the root cause and treat it with manual therapy, posture correction, and targeted strengthening.
symptoms: Persistent lower back or neck pain
Pain that worsens with sitting or desk work
Stiffness or reduced flexibility through the spine
benefits: Addresses the root cause, not just the pain flare-up
Long-term relief instead of repeat short-term treatment
services.recovery: Most patients see meaningful improvement within 4–6 weeks of consistent therapy.

services.name: Neurological Rehabilitation
services.tagline: Rebuilding movement and independence after a neurological event
services.overview: For patients recovering from stroke, nerve injury, or other neurological conditions, our therapists focus on restoring movement, balance, and functional independence through patient-paced, hands-on rehabilitation.
symptoms: Weakness or reduced coordination on one side of the body
services.recovery: Neurological rehab is typically a longer-term program, reviewed and adjusted every 4 weeks.

faqs.question: Can I walk in without an appointment?
faqs.answer: Walk-ins are welcome when a therapist is free, but booking ahead guarantees your slot, especially during evening hours.

faqs.question: What happens in the first session?
faqs.answer: Your first visit is a hands-on assessment of the injured area and your overall movement, followed by an initial manual therapy session and a written recovery plan.

faqs.question: Do you accept insurance or is it pay-per-visit?
faqs.answer: We operate on direct pay-per-visit billing. We can provide receipts and reports for patients seeking insurance reimbursement separately.

faqs.question: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.answer: It depends on the injury — sports strains often resolve in 3–6 sessions, while post-surgical and chronic conditions typically run 6–12 weeks with progress reviewed each visit.

faqs.question: Do I need a doctor's referral to book an appointment?
faqs.answer: No referral is required — you can book an assessment directly, though we're glad to coordinate with your surgeon or physician if you have one.

blogPosts.title: Manual Therapy vs. Exercise-Based Rehab: What's the Difference?
blogPosts.excerpt: Exercise sheets and hands-on manual therapy aren't interchangeable. Here's what each one actually does — and why most real recovery plans need both.
blogPosts.author: Vignesh Raman
content: A printed exercise sheet and a hands-on manual therapy session are treating two different problems, even though both get filed under "physiotherapy."
Exercise-based rehab builds strength and endurance over time — it's essential, but it can't do much for a joint that's mechanically restricted or a muscle that's locked in spasm.

Manual therapy — joint mobilization, soft-tissue release, hands-on stretching — addresses restriction directly, often producing a change in range of motion within a single session that exercise alone would take weeks to reach.
The two aren't competing approaches. Most of our recovery plans use manual therapy to unlock movement early, then layer in progressive exercise to make that movement strong and durable.
If your current plan is exercise sheets only, ask whether hands-on treatment is part of it — for a lot of injuries, it should be.
